# mediamix

Composable media transforms and attribution path construction for R.

mediamix turns raw marketing data into model-ready features: media spend
into carryover- and saturation-adjusted regressors, and raw event logs
into attributed customer journeys.

Use it if you fit your own marketing mix model, whether in
[`lm()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html), `glmnet`, `brms`, Stan or a
tidymodels workflow, or if you need customer journeys and attribution
built from a raw event log.

It is a preprocessing, feature-engineering and reporting package, not a
modelling engine. [`lm()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html), `glmnet`
and `brms` fit models better than a marketing package would, and `tune`
does hyperparameter search properly. mediamix does the steps in front of
the model and the decomposition after it, with the methodological
details that usually get skipped written into the API.

Documentation, walkthroughs and worked examples are on the package
website, <https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/>.

## What it offers

The full MMM frameworks (Robyn in R; Meridian and PyMC-Marketing in
Python) bundle transforms, a model, an optimiser and reporting into one
pipeline. mediamix provides those pieces separately, for use around a
model you choose:

- [`step_adstock()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/step_adstock.md)
  carries filter state across the train/test boundary, so carryover,
  saturation and a model penalty can be tuned jointly in one
  `tune_bayes()` call with no rows lost.
- [`marginal_roi()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/marginal_roi.md)
  re-runs the whole transform on a 1% larger budget, the definition used
  by Jin et al. (2017) and by Meridian. The common shortcut, a curve’s
  slope times the kernel’s first weight, understates slow channels
  several-fold.
- [`allocate_budget()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/allocate_budget.md)
  splits a budget across channels to maximise the media response a
  fitted model predicts, rescaling each channel’s series so its
  flighting is kept. It compares every spend level of every channel on a
  grid, so an S-shaped channel that returns little on its first
  increments is not left unfunded.
  [`simulate_plan()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/simulate_plan.md)
  and
  [`reallocate()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/reallocate.md)
  test a single move through the same curves.
- [`tune_carryover()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/tune_carryover.md)
  and, for every channel at once inside one model with controls,
  [`tune_carryover_joint()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/tune_carryover_joint.md)
  score candidates on held-out KPI with forward-only resampling and
  report the one-standard-error choice alongside the minimum.
- [`block_bootstrap()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/block_bootstrap.md)
  resamples runs of weeks to put intervals on ROI, marginal ROI or
  anything else you compute.
- [`build_paths()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/build_paths.md)
  turns a raw event log into journeys with every construction choice an
  argument, and accounts for the conversions that filtering leaves
  unattributable.
- [`attribute()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/attribute.md)
  runs five rule-based credit schemes and an order-1 Markov
  removal-effect model side by side, and
  [`attribution_spread()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/attribution_spread.md)
  reports how much the answer depends on the choice.
- [`decay_from_half_life()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/decay_vocabulary.md)
  and
  [`half_life()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/decay_vocabulary.md)
  translate between a decay coefficient and the half-life practitioners
  talk in, and
  [`effective_window()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/decay_vocabulary.md)
  gives the number of periods that hold 90% of the effect; both halves
  of the package use this one vocabulary.

## Scope

| In | Out | Because |
|----|----|----|
| Adstock and saturation transforms | Model fitting | `lm`, `glmnet`, `brms` already exist |
| Carryover selection by cross-validation | Bespoke hyperparameter optimisers | `tune` does this properly |
| Journey construction from event logs | Higher-order Markov chains | `ChannelAttribution` does them in C++ |
| Rule-based credit and order-1 Markov removal effects | Causal incrementality | Requires experiments, not logs |
| Contribution, ROI, counterfactual marginal ROI and budget allocation | Allocation under parameter uncertainty | [`allocate_budget()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/allocate_budget.md) takes point estimates; [`block_bootstrap()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/block_bootstrap.md) measures how far they move |
| Media data diagnostics | Generic regression diagnostics | `broom`, `performance` |

[`as_channel_paths()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/as_channel_paths.md)
exports journeys straight into `ChannelAttribution`’s format, for
higher-order models and very large path tables.

## Installation

mediamix is not yet on CRAN. Install the development version from
GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("elkronos/mediamix")
```

`pak` does not build vignettes for packages installed from GitHub, so
[`vignette("carryover")`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/articles/carryover.md)
and the others are not available after this install. Read them on the
[package website](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/), or install with
`remotes::install_github("elkronos/mediamix", build_vignettes = TRUE)`.

mediamix imports `cli` and `rlang` for its messages and `data.table` for
the attribution half, where event logs get large. It has no compiled
code. `recipes`, `dials` and the rest of tidymodels are in `Suggests`
and registered conditionally, so the transforms work equally well from a
Stan or `brms` workflow that will never touch them.

## Example

### Media mix modelling

`mm_weekly` holds three years of weekly spend on five channels, with
price and revenue, for three geographies. It was simulated from known
carryover and saturation parameters, kept in its `"truth"` attribute, so
every estimate below can be checked. The example uses the north
geography:

``` r

library(mediamix)
data(mm_weekly)
truth <- attr(mm_weekly, "truth")

north <- mm_weekly[mm_weekly$geo == "north", ]
channels <- c("tv", "video", "search", "social", "display")
controls <- data.frame(week = seq_len(nrow(north)), price = north$price,
                       seasonality = north$seasonality,
                       holiday = north$holiday)
```

It is tempting to choose decay by asking which transformed series is
best-behaved. That criterion has no dependent variable in it, so it
ranks filters by how hard they smooth rather than by anything about the
outcome.
[`tune_carryover_joint()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/tune_carryover_joint.md)
scores each candidate by how well a model with every channel and the
controls predicts *held-out* revenue, so no channel is credited with
another’s effect. The default model is ordinary least squares; `fit_fn`
and `predict_fn` take any other.

``` r

joint <- tune_carryover_joint(north[channels], north$revenue,
                              controls = controls)
rbind(estimate = joint$best$decay, truth = truth$decay[channels])
#>            tv video search social display
#> estimate 0.80   0.5   0.65   0.55    0.60
#> truth    0.85   0.7   0.15   0.45    0.55
```

Of the five, video and search miss by more than 0.1. Search’s
cross-validation profile is almost flat: the data does not identify its
carryover, which `plot(joint)` makes visible and a bare point estimate
would hide. Carryover is weakly identified in most real data, which is
why the one-standard-error rule (Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman, 2009)
is reported alongside, as `joint$best_1se`.

The joint search does not tune saturation, so to keep the example short
the model below uses the parameters `mm_weekly` was simulated from:
geometric adstock (Broadbent, 1979) followed by a Hill curve (Hill,
1910), which
[`media_transform()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/media_transform.md)
applies in that order.
[`transform_plan()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/transform_plan.md)
does the same for every channel of a plan, each with its own entry in
`spec`. Any model can go on top; here it is
[`lm()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html) with the controls.
[`contributions()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/contributions.md)
splits the fitted revenue into one part per channel and a baseline, and
[`roi()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/roi.md) divides
each channel’s contribution by its spend:

``` r

spec <- lapply(stats::setNames(channels, channels), function(ch) list(
  adstock = list(decay = truth$decay[[ch]]),
  saturation = list(half_max = truth$half_max[[ch]],
                    shape = truth$shape[[ch]])
))
media <- transform_plan(north, spec)[channels]
fit <- lm(north$revenue ~ ., data = cbind(media, controls))
contrib <- contributions(media, fit, index = north$date)
roi(contrib, north[channels])
#>   channel contribution  spend   roi
#> 1  social       132709  36716 3.614
#> 2  search       208307  74560 2.794
#> 3   video       102461  53248 1.924
#> 4 display        40853  26937 1.517
#> 5      tv       349629 266978 1.310
```

Every channel returns more than it costs on average. The main results
have [`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) methods in
one consistent, colour-vision-checked style; here is the decomposition
week by week:

``` r

plot(contrib)
```

![](reference/figures/README-contributions-1.png)

Average ROI is a scorecard; marginal ROI is the decision variable.
[`marginal_roi()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/marginal_roi.md)
computes it the way Jin et al. (2017) and Meridian define it, as the
extra response from a 1% larger budget divided by the extra spend, by
re-running carryover and saturation rather than differentiating a curve:

``` r

tv <- marginal_roi(north$tv, coefficient = coef(fit)[["tv"]],
                   adstock = list(decay = truth$decay[["tv"]]),
                   saturation = list(half_max = truth$half_max[["tv"]],
                                     shape = truth$shape[["tv"]]))
tv
#>    spend contribution  roi  mroi
#> 1 266978       349629 1.31 1.253
```

Television’s next pound returns 1.25, close to its average of 1.31. The
tempting shortcut, the curve’s slope times the kernel’s first weight,
gives 0.21 for this channel: it counts only the week of spend and
discards the 85% of the effect that arrives later.

[`block_bootstrap()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/block_bootstrap.md)
puts intervals on any of these numbers. On `mm_weekly` they are wide,
which is the point: see the [budget
walkthrough](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/articles/budget-walkthrough.html)
for how that changes a recommendation, and how its answer compares with
the truth the data was simulated from.

### Attribution

Attribution tools such as `ChannelAttribution` consume `"a > b > c"`
strings with conversion counts attached; producing those strings is left
to the analyst. That step usually ends up as a `group_by()` and a
`paste(collapse = " > ")`, and that loses a great deal.

On `mm_events`, the package’s 20,799-event synthetic log:

|                                    | journeys | mean length |
|:-----------------------------------|---------:|------------:|
| naive one-path-per-customer        |    5,400 |        3.85 |
| split on conversion                |    6,105 |        3.39 |
| \+ collapse consecutive duplicates |    6,105 |        2.83 |

The last row is
[`build_paths()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/build_paths.md)
with its defaults: 13% more journeys than the first row, and 27%
shorter. Journey counts and lengths feed a Markov transition matrix
directly, so those are not rounding differences. Each of these choices
is an argument to
[`build_paths()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/build_paths.md):

``` r

paths <- build_paths(
  mm_events,
  id = "customer_id", channel = "channel", timestamp = "timestamp",
  conversion = "conversion", value = "value",
  lookback = 30,                       # or read it off conversion_lag()
  split_on = c("conversion", "gap"), gap = 30,
  collapse_repeats = TRUE,
  keep_null_paths = TRUE,              # Markov removal effects need these
  direct = "label"
)
```

[`build_paths()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/build_paths.md)
handles the things that go wrong between an event log and a set of
journeys: journey splitting, lookback windows, non-converting paths,
direct, none and missing channels, consecutive duplicates, duplicate
events, timestamps that do not parse, deterministic tie-breaking, and
accounting for conversions that filtering leaves unattributable. Each is
an argument, not an assumption.

Dropping direct traffic can strip a converting journey of every
touchpoint it had. mediamix fixes the conversion facts before any
filtering, so those conversions are counted and reported as
`conversions_unattributable` rather than quietly shrinking the
denominator.

Any single credit rule gives you a number. Several give you the range
that number could have been.
[`attribute()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/attribute.md)
runs five heuristic rules and an order-1 Markov removal-effect model
(Anderl et al., 2016). The four channels whose share varies most:

``` r

shares <- attribute(paths)
spread <- attribution_spread(shares)
head(spread, 4)
#>       channel min_share max_share mean_share spread first_last_ratio
#> 1     display   0.07187    0.2904     0.1739 0.2185           4.0406
#> 2 paid_search   0.09230    0.2725     0.1840 0.1802           0.3387
#> 3       email   0.05655    0.1831     0.1237 0.1266           0.3088
#> 4      social   0.11638    0.2207     0.1657 0.1043           1.8966
```

``` r

plot(shares)
```

![](reference/figures/README-attribution-1.png)

Display’s share runs from 7% to 29% depending only on the convention
chosen. That channel has not been measured; it has been assigned a
number. The Markov share falls inside the heuristic range for 6 of 7
channels here: a data-driven convention narrows the argument without
ending it.

Rule-based attribution is a bookkeeping convention, not a causal
estimate. It divides observed conversions among observed touchpoints by
a rule you chose; it cannot tell you what would have happened if a
channel had not run, because that outcome is not in the log. Only an
experiment answers that.

## Where to go next

From first steps to deeper material:

- [`vignette("mediamix")`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/articles/mediamix.md):
  getting started, from raw data to contributions and ROI.
- The [budget
  walkthrough](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/articles/budget-walkthrough.html):
  one budget question from weekly spend to a recommendation, checked
  against the parameters the data was simulated from.
- [`vignette("carryover")`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/articles/carryover.md):
  choosing decay and lag by cross-validation, and why five correlated
  channels make it harder.
- [`vignette("tidymodels")`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/articles/tidymodels.md):
  joint tuning of transform and model parameters, with recipe steps that
  carry adstock across the train/test boundary.
- [`vignette("journeys")`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/articles/journeys.md):
  building journeys from event logs.
- [`vignette("spine")`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/articles/spine.md):
  carryover and credit are the same idea, the geometric kernel run
  forward from spend for adstock and backward from a conversion for
  time-decay credit.
- [Methods and
  references](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/articles/methodology.html):
  the method behind each function and where it comes from.
- [How mediamix relates to other
  tools](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/articles/comparison.html):
  Robyn, Meridian, PyMC-Marketing and ChannelAttribution.

The walkthrough, the methods page and the comparison are on the website
only; the vignettes also ship with the package.

## References

Anderl, E., Becker, I., von Wangenheim, F. and Schumann, J. H. (2016).
Mapping the customer journey: Lessons learned from graph-based online
attribution modeling. *International Journal of Research in Marketing*,
33(3), 457–474. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijresmar.2016.03.001>

Broadbent, S. (1979). One way TV advertisements work. *Journal of the
Market Research Society*, 21(3), 139–166.

Hastie, T., Tibshirani, R. and Friedman, J. (2009). *The Elements of
Statistical Learning* (2nd ed.). Springer.
<https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-84858-7>

Hill, A. V. (1910). The possible effects of the aggregation of the
molecules of haemoglobin on its dissociation curves. *The Journal of
Physiology*, 40, iv–vii.
<https://doi.org/10.1113/jphysiol.1910.sp001386>

Jin, Y., Wang, Y., Sun, Y., Chan, D. and Koehler, J. (2017). *Bayesian
methods for media mix modeling with carryover and shape effects.* Google
Inc.

# Package index

## Check the data

Find collinear, flat or dark channels and inconsistent costs before
fitting anything.

- [`diagnose_media()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/diagnose_media.md)
  : Diagnose media data before modelling
- [`plot(`*`<mm_diagnosis>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/plot.mm_diagnosis.md)
  : Plot media diagnostics

## Carryover (adstock)

Spread each period’s media forward in time, and translate decay into a
half-life.

- [`adstock_geometric()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/adstock_geometric.md)
  : Geometric adstock
- [`adstock_weibull()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/adstock_weibull.md)
  : Weibull adstock
- [`adstock_weights_delayed()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/adstock_delayed.md)
  [`adstock_delayed()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/adstock_delayed.md)
  : Delayed adstock
- [`adstock_filter()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/adstock_filter.md)
  : Adstock with an arbitrary kernel
- [`adstock_weights()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/adstock_weights.md)
  : Geometric adstock weights
- [`adstock_weights_weibull()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/adstock_weights_weibull.md)
  : Weibull adstock weights
- [`adstock_state()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/adstock_state.md)
  : Terminal adstock state
- [`adstock_steady_state()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/adstock_steady_state.md)
  : Steady-state starting value for an adstock filter
- [`decay_from_half_life()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/decay_vocabulary.md)
  [`half_life()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/decay_vocabulary.md)
  [`effective_window()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/decay_vocabulary.md)
  : Carryover decay vocabulary

## Saturation

Diminishing returns as media pressure grows.

- [`saturate_hill()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/saturation.md)
  [`saturate_exponential()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/saturation.md)
  [`saturate_michaelis_menten()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/saturation.md)
  [`saturate_power()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/saturation.md)
  [`saturate()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/saturation.md)
  : Saturation curves

## Composing transforms

Apply carryover then saturation to one channel or to every channel of a
plan, and convert Robyn’s hyperparameters to these arguments.

- [`media_transform()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/media_transform.md)
  : Adstock then saturate, in that order
- [`transform_plan()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/transform_plan.md)
  : Transform every channel of a media plan
- [`from_robyn()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/from_robyn.md)
  : Convert Robyn hyperparameters to mediamix arguments

## Choosing carryover parameters

Score candidate decays and lags by how well a model predicts held-out
KPI, with seasonality terms as controls.

- [`tune_carryover()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/tune_carryover.md)
  : Select carryover parameters by cross-validation against a KPI
- [`tune_carryover_joint()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/tune_carryover_joint.md)
  : Tune every channel's carryover jointly, inside one model
- [`plot(`*`<mm_carryover>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/plot_carryover.md)
  [`plot(`*`<mm_carryover_joint>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/plot_carryover.md)
  : Plot a carryover cross-validation profile
- [`fit_ols()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/fit_ols.md)
  [`predict(`*`<mm_ols>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/fit_ols.md)
  [`coef(`*`<mm_ols>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/fit_ols.md)
  [`fitted(`*`<mm_ols>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/fit_ols.md)
  [`print(`*`<mm_ols>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/fit_ols.md)
  : Default linear fitter for carryover tuning
- [`rmse()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/metrics.md)
  [`mae()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/metrics.md) :
  Root mean squared error and mean absolute error
- [`fourier_terms()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/seasonality.md)
  [`holiday_flags()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/seasonality.md)
  : Seasonality controls for a model frame

## Tuning with tidymodels

Recipe steps and tuning parameters for tuning carryover, saturation and
a model penalty together.

- [`step_adstock()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/step_adstock.md)
  : Adstock transformation as a recipe step
- [`step_adstock_channels()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/step_adstock_channels.md)
  : One adstock step per channel
- [`step_saturation()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/step_saturation.md)
  : Saturation transformation as a recipe step
- [`carryover_decay()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/mediamix_params.md)
  [`carryover_max_lag()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/mediamix_params.md)
  [`carryover_shape()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/mediamix_params.md)
  [`carryover_scale()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/mediamix_params.md)
  [`carryover_peak()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/mediamix_params.md)
  [`saturation_half_max()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/mediamix_params.md)
  [`saturation_shape()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/mediamix_params.md)
  : Tuning parameters for media transforms

## Contributions and return on investment

Turn a fitted model into channel contributions, average and marginal
return, and response curves.

- [`contributions()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/contributions.md)
  : Decompose predicted KPI into channel contributions
- [`plot(`*`<mm_contributions>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/plot.mm_contributions.md)
  : Plot a contribution decomposition
- [`roi()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/roi.md)
  [`mroi()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/roi.md) :
  Return on investment and marginal return
- [`marginal_roi()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/marginal_roi.md)
  : Average and marginal return by counterfactual simulation
- [`response_curve()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/response_curve.md)
  [`spend_for()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/response_curve.md)
  : Response curve for a channel
- [`plot(`*`<mm_response_curve>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/plot.mm_response_curve.md)
  : Plot a response curve

## Uncertainty

Put intervals on any statistic by resampling blocks of consecutive
periods.

- [`block_bootstrap()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/block_bootstrap.md)
  : Moving block bootstrap for time-series statistics
- [`plot(`*`<mm_bootstrap>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/plot.mm_bootstrap.md)
  : Plot bootstrap intervals

## Budget planning

Simulate a plan through the fitted transforms, move budget between
channels, and split a total budget across channels.

- [`simulate_plan()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/simulate_plan.md)
  : Predicted media response of a plan
- [`reallocate()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/reallocate.md)
  : Move spend between two channels of a plan
- [`allocate_budget()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/allocate_budget.md)
  : Allocate a budget across channels
- [`plot(`*`<mm_allocation>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/plot.mm_allocation.md)
  : Plot a budget allocation

## Journey construction

Turn a raw event log into customer journeys, and combine or subset them.

- [`build_paths()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/build_paths.md)
  : Build customer journeys from a raw event log
- [`bind_paths()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/bind_paths.md)
  [`rbind(`*`<mm_paths>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/bind_paths.md)
  : Combine journey tables
- [`` `[`( ``*`<mm_paths>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/sub-.mm_paths.md)
  : Subset a journey table

## Journey diagnostics

Describe a journey table, including how long conversions take, before
choosing a lookback or a credit rule.

- [`path_summary()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/path_summary.md)
  : Journey table summary
- [`path_lengths()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/path_lengths.md)
  : Journey length distribution
- [`channel_positions()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/channel_positions.md)
  : Where each channel sits in the journey
- [`assisted_conversions()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/assisted_conversions.md)
  : Assisted conversion matrix
- [`top_paths()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/top_paths.md)
  : Most common journeys
- [`conversion_lag()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/conversion_lag.md)
  : Conversion lag distribution
- [`path_diagnostics()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/path_diagnostics.md)
  : Run every journey diagnostic at once

## Attribution

Credit conversions to channels by rule or by Markov removal effects,
compare the rules, and export journeys to ChannelAttribution.

- [`credit_linear()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/credit.md)
  [`credit_first()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/credit.md)
  [`credit_last()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/credit.md)
  [`credit_position()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/credit.md)
  [`credit_time_decay()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/credit.md)
  [`credit_custom()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/credit.md)
  : Assign conversion credit across a journey
- [`markov_removal()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/markov_removal.md)
  : Markov-chain removal effects
- [`attribute()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/attribute.md)
  : Attribute conversions to channels under several rules at once
- [`attribution_spread()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/attribution_spread.md)
  : Range of each channel's share across attribution rules
- [`plot(`*`<mm_attribution>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/plot.mm_attribution.md)
  : Plot attribution shares across rules
- [`plot(`*`<mm_attribution_intervals>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/plot.mm_attribution_intervals.md)
  [`plot(`*`<mm_attribution_segments>`*`)`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/plot.mm_attribution_intervals.md)
  : Plot attribution shares with intervals or by segment
- [`as_channel_paths()`](https://elkronos.github.io/mediamix/reference/as_channel_paths.md)
  : Export journeys in ChannelAttribution's format
